evidence_frontier: Exp021 (PNN-v1-Exp021) evaluated two compression candidates on ECG200: w8 (4,278 parameters) achieved 887 aggregate Q.ANT correct predictions (10 fewer than the Alpha5 w16 control's 897), while w12 performed worse. The w8 result is the current frontier for local‑width compression. No confirmation of this boundary has yet been performed on an independent seed set.
analysis: Observation: The w8 compression candidate loses exactly 10 correct predictions relative to the w16 control on the original seed set (100 test samples). Observation: The gate used in Exp021 was a floating‑point retain_alpha5 decision; the next preregistered question calls for an integer‑count gate to test reproducibility. Observation: The control architecture (Alpha5 w16) remains active and unchanged. Observation: All prior experiments used the Q.ANT CPU/software simulation backend and did not claim physical photonic performance.
hypothesis: When evaluated on a fresh, independent set of random seeds, the Alpha5 w8 compression candidate will achieve aggregate Q.ANT correct predictions no more than 10 fewer than the Alpha5 w16 control on the ECG200 test set (i.e., candidate_correct ≥ control_correct − 10).

proposal.title: Confirmation of the w8 Local‑Width Compression Boundary on ECG200
proposal.research_question: Is the w8 compression boundary reproducible within a 10‑prediction tolerance of the Alpha5 w16 control on a fresh seed set?
proposal.rationale: Exp021 showed a 10‑prediction gap for w8 on a single seed configuration. Confirming this boundary with an integer‑count gate on independent seeds will validate the robustness of the w8 compression rule before any further width reductions are explored.

procedure: Generate a fresh preregistered list of N=5 random seeds (different from Exp021).
For each seed, train an Alpha5 model with local_width=8 (w8) on the ECG200 training set (100 samples).
For each seed, also instantiate the Alpha5 w16 control (unchanged architecture) and evaluate it on the same training procedure for consistency.
Using each seed, evaluate both w8 candidate and w16 control on the ECG200 test set (100 samples) and record the number of correct Q.ANT predictions.
Aggregate correct counts across all 5 seeds (total predictions = 5 × 100 = 500) for candidate and control.
Apply the confirmation gate: candidate_correct ≥ control_correct − 10.

success_criteria.description: On the fresh 5‑seed evaluation (500 total test predictions), the w8 candidate must achieve at least (control_correct − 10) aggregate correct predictions. The denominator for the gate is 500 predictions.

proposal.risks: Potential stochastic variance could cause the candidate to fall more than 10 predictions short, leading to a failed confirmation. Training on a small dataset may amplify seed sensitivity. The integer‑count gate is strict; any systematic bias in the simulation backend could affect reproducibility.
